question: If artificial practices fall short of the uncreated reality, why are they still prescribed at all?
premises: Artificial practices are not worth even a sixteenth part of the uncreated reality.
Their value is therefore radically limited in comparison with the uncreated.
Even so, they may still be prescribed here by rule for a certain purpose.
inference: Constructed practices have no ultimate parity with the uncreated, yet they can still be conventionally prescribed within a regulated framework.
uncertainties: The verse states that prescription remains but does not specify its exact pedagogical purpose.
plain_english: Therefore these artificial practices are not worth even a sixteenth part of that uncreated reality. Still, O Goddess, they are prescribed here by rule.
